title: Service-floor & price-anchoring experiment for Private/VPC on‑prem bundles
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run a 6-week pricing and packaging experiment to test a service-floor (minimum uptime/response SLAs) plus price‑anchoring mechanics for Private/VPC and on‑prem bundles. Objective: determine willingness-to-pay for explicit uptime credits, prioritized security validations (KMS/HSM + SOC2 attestations), and expedited upgrade paths. Output: recommended price bands, SLA language, support tiers matrix, and a go/no-go decision for pilot contracts.
success_metrics: signed pilot deals >= 3 with ARR >= $120k each
>70% NPS for security/upgrade experience among pilot customers
reduction in SLA escalation tickets by 30% after introducing uptime crediting
assumptions: customers value written uptime credits when paired with expedited patch SLAs
security artifacts materially reduce procurement friction for regulated buyers
ops cost for emergency patching can be priced as credits without eroding margins
pricing_hypotheses: H1: a 10% premium for a guaranteed 99.9% uptime floor with 10% credit on missed SLA converts at higher rate than a generic subscription
H2: bundling KMS/HSM attestation + 30-day prioritized hotfix reduces procurement review time by 40% and justifies a $Xk uplift
H3: offering an upgrade cadence guarantee (quarterly security-only, biannual feature upgrades) will reduce customer churn in year 1
timeline: 2026-03-17: price anchoring experiments instrumented in commercial proposals
constraints_and_risks: Ops capacity for emergency patch windows may require a dedicated on-call pool
Legal review time for new SLA wording could push pilots out
Risk of over-promising uptime without adequate redundancy in some on‑prem configurations
decisions_needed: authorize price anchoring levels and acceptable margin floors
approve SLA credit formula and refund mechanics
scope minimum security deliverables for an eligible bundled price
notes: We should avoid coupling feature-only upgrades to security patches for the highest-tier; customers asked for explicit separation during interviews
Prefer committing to % credit of monthly fee rather than pro-rata compute refunds to simplify ops
